question_text: A tissue has 1024 cells at a given time. How many cycles of mitosis had the original single parent cell undergone?

steps.label: The doubling rule
lines: Each cycle of mitosis doubles the number of

lines.text: After n cycles, number of cells = 2ⁿ

steps.why: Mitosis gives two daughter cells from one, so the count is always a power of two. Writing 1024 as a power of 2 turns the question into reading off the index.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that the tissue started from ONE cell, so no extra doubling is added.
steps.memory_tip: Powers of 2 worth knowing: 2⁵ = 32, 2¹⁰ = 1024, 2²⁰ is about a million.
steps.margin_note: Two short lines: the rule, then 1024 written as a power of 2.

steps.label: The answer

lines.text: n = 10 — the parent cell has gone through 10 cycles of mitosis.

steps.why: Once 1024 is written as 2¹⁰ the index IS the number of cycles, so the answer needs no further working. The book's key gives 10 cycles of mitosis, which matches.
steps.memory_tip: The power is the number of cycles.
steps.margin_note: One boxed line. Do not write more.

insider_note: Show 1024 = 2¹⁰ in your script. An answer of 10 with no working can be read as a guess.
